label: hero v2
goal: Buy one Trail Backpack with standard delivery. Your details: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city Testville, ZIP 99999, country United States. Pay by card: name on card Alex Morgan, card number 4111 1111 1111 1111, expiry 12/30, security code 123. Agree to the terms of sale. You do not want newsletters or promotions.

outcome.reason: The order is confirmed by the payment oracle.

findings.page: Your cart - Pine and Peak Outfitters
findings.problem: A newsletter dialog opened automatically on arrival at the cart and grabbed focus; I had to find and close it before continuing, and it was unwanted promotion.
After activating Add to cart there is no page change; only a status message says the item was added, and the cart link count is easy to miss.

The labels for fields are separate text next to unnamed-state inputs; required fields are not marked and delivery radios show no checked state until pressed, so it was unclear whether standard delivery was preselected.
After pressing Pay there was no announcement or status of processing; the page looked unchanged until I re-read it, with a raw URL as the page title (Loading http://127.0.0.1...).
The card fields sit in separate iframes, and the PayPal button iframe exposes only a link; the Cardholder Name field is marked optional though requested.

findings.page: Your cart - Pine and Peak Outfitters
findings.problem: A newsletter dialog opened automatically on arrival at the cart and grabbed focus; I had to find and close it before continuing, and it was unwanted promotion.
After activating Add to cart there is no page change; only a status message says the item was added, and the cart link count is easy to miss.

The labels for fields are separate text next to unnamed-state inputs; required fields are not marked and delivery radios show no checked state until pressed, so it was unclear whether standard delivery was preselected.
After pressing Pay there was no announcement or status of processing; the page looked unchanged until I re-read it, with a raw URL as the page title (Loading http://127.0.0.1...).
The card fields sit in separate iframes, and the PayPal button iframe exposes only a link; the Cardholder Name field is marked optional though requested.
